  • Method Details

    • $interceptorRegistrations

      @Internal default List<BeanRegistration<Interceptor<?,?>>> $interceptorRegistrations()
      The interceptor registrations that were resolved for this proxy.

      The scenario this exists for is an advised bean that also declares lifecycle advice:

      @Retention(RUNTIME)
@Around
@InterceptorBinding(kind = InterceptorKind.POST_CONSTRUCT)
@InterceptorBinding(kind = InterceptorKind.PRE_DESTROY)
@interface Tracked {}

@Singleton @Tracked
class MyBean { @PostConstruct void init() {} @PreDestroy void close() {} }

      The proxy constructor is given the registrations that match the target's bindings and keeps them, so post-construct and pre-destroy interception select from the same set the proxy already uses for its methods, and a @Prototype interceptor is one instance for the whole life of one target. Destruction in particular has no other route to them: it runs with a fresh resolution context, and the proxy instance is the only thing that survives from creation to destruction.

      Proxies whose target declares no lifecycle binding, and proxies generated before this existed, keep the empty default; the runtime then resolves interceptors by binding as it always did.

      Returns:
      The retained interceptor registrations, never null
      Since:
      5.2.0
